title.narrative: CDRC003.4 ACM DRC_Burundi 2025_2026 (lead)

description.narrative: The government of Burundi declared a state of emergency on the 17th of December. As part of this emergency declaration, a joint InterAgency Flash Appeal developed by UNHCR in coordination with the Government and Partners was released, with eight partners appealing for a combined US$33.2 million to respond to 90,000 new arrivals over a four-month period. UNHCR has launched a four-month emergency appeal for the period December 2025 through March 2026. Under this appeal UNHCR is requesting US$47.2 million to support the immediate and ongoing response to IDPs in eastern DRC, reinforce preparedness, and sustain life-saving protection and assistance for refugees and returnees arriving in Burundi as well the broader region. Priority sectors: WASH, Shelter/NFIs, Protection and multipurpose cash assistance (MPC) as a modality to meet the most urgent needs of displaced families. Beneficiaries will be targeted with a combination of activities from different sectors. On the DRC side of the border, the response will focus on Uvira terriory, with the following health areas being targeted by partners: Kalundu State Health Area, Kalundu CEPAC Health Area, and Kalundu Catholic Health Area, Kiliba CEPAC, Kasenga and Kagando Health Areas, Hongero, Kilibas Ondes, Runingu and Ndunda. In Burundi, the response will focus on the reception sites close to the border, such as Cishemere and Kansenga camps. Where possible, JR partners will coordinate with the aim of complementarity and/or targeting the same beneficiaries, for example in Cishemere camp in Burundi. Importantly, the response will continue to monitor the flow of refugees. It is to be expected that the Burundian authorities will move refugees to more permanent camps in the east of the country. Partners are prepared to be flexible and respond where the needs are highest.

title.narrative: Adaptations to JR (ACC-I2)
Number of adaptations in the design and/or implementation of the JR, as a result of the input from beneficiaries.

description.narrative: Active participation of beneficiaries could lead to concrete proposals in programme design and/or on how to improve existing implementation. In the activity description/comment field, indicate how this input from beneficiaries is gathered (planned) and at mid/end-term stage, what input was received from beneficiaries and to which adaptations this has led.

comment.narrative: Adjustments to the project will be implemented based on feedback received through established feedback channels, including hotlines, PDMs, or routine consultations conducted throughout the project's duration. The lead and JR partners will also closely monitor the implementation of the recent Hamas/Israel agreed and adapt the program according to the developments on the ground, humanitarian access and changing prices of goods and services that might occur.

title.narrative: Participation (ACC-I1)
Number of crisis-affected people who are also involved in the design, implementation, monitoring and/or evaluation of the programme

description.narrative: Participation is defined as the involvement of crisis-affected people in one or more phases of the programme: assessment, design, implementation, monitoring or evaluation. Participation does not take place when activities are carried out in exchange for a salary of 'in-kind' payment unless the affected people are involved in decision-making processes and have an impact on decisions that affect them. Please describe in the actvity description what this involvement specifically entails and in which phase of the program conflict-affected people are involved.

comment.narrative: Communities are actively involved at every stage of the project cycle. The project design is informed by participatory consultations conducted with individuals during the Rapid Needs Assessments. Additionally, Participatory Monitoring and Accountability Mechanisms will ensure that rightsholders and local stakeholders remain engaged in monitoring and providing feedback, empowering them to contribute continuously to the adjustment and improvement of interventions.

title.narrative: Joint learning (CI-I3)
Are there one or more learning activities conducted? YES/NO

description.narrative: Tick the box with a YES if you have a minimum of one joint learning. Otherwise NO. Joint learning: when two or more (local) partners have a workshop, course or learning visits etc The standard real time evaluations, end evaluation and kick-off/midd-ter meetings do not count. If yes, please elaborate in narrative.

comment.narrative: The lead will organise a RRTR to promote learning and peer review among the partner of the joint response.

title.narrative: Sharing resources, e.g. warehousing, transport (CI-I2)
Is there one or more instances of sharing resources ? YES/NO

description.narrative: Tick the box with a YES if you have a minimum of one sharing of resources. Otherwise NO. Sharing: When two or more (local) partners share an office, means of tranport, a warehouse or sharing of staff/consultants. If yes, please elaborate in narrative.

comment.narrative: Several DRA partners will share offices with their local partners in Uvira

title.narrative: Alignment on approaches, e.g. shared tools and frameworks, monitoring (CI-I4)
Are there (monitoring) tools and frameworks shared amongst and newly used by partners? YES/NO

description.narrative: Tick the box with a YES if you have a minimum of one tool or framework shared and used. Otherwise NO. You can only count if the tool/framework shared is used for the first time by one or more other partners. If yes, please elaborate in narrative.

comment.narrative: Several DRA partners will use harmonized beneficiary criteria and selections processes as they are working in the same areas and transit camps

title.narrative: Geographical complementarity/ coverage (CI-I6)
Are two or more partners carrying out joint programming in one geographical areas within the JR? YES/NO

description.narrative: Tick the box with a YES if you have a minimum of two partners carrying out joint programming in one geographical area. Otherwise NO. Geographical area defined at propsal stage. If yes, please elaborate in narrative.

comment.narrative: Yes, several partners will implement integrated joint programming in the same geographical areas of the JR.

title.narrative: Short-term livelihood support (FSC-I1)
Number of people provided with resources to protect and start rebuilding livelihood assets

description.narrative: Resources that enable people to protect and rebuild their livelihood assets include seeds, livestock, tools, business grant, etc. Any kind of transfer modality (in-kind, voucher, restricted cash) and combination thereof to support, protect and enable the restoration/protection/access of/to livelihood assets.

comment.narrative: Distribute cash-for-food assistance of €85/HH/month for 3 months to 500 HH. Cash is delivered in local currency.

title.narrative: Capacity Building (reach) (LOC-I3)
Number of national and local actors supported with capacity-building

description.narrative: Please mention here the total number of national and local actors that received capacity-building support during implementation. In case more than one individual from a national/local actor participate in the capacity building activities, please only count this actor once. Note that this does not include local offices of INGOs.

comment.narrative: The joint response will be implemented together with 9 local partner that will be supported with capacity strenghtening

% of budget that went to national and local actors

description.narrative: This concerns Local Implementing Partner Costs. Please divide Local Implementing Partner Costs by the Grand Total Budget (incl ICR) to calculate this percentage. Note that this does not include local offices of INGOs.

comment.narrative: 44% of the budget will be implemented by local partners

title.narrative: Capacity Building (localisation) (LOC-I2)
% of budget spent on capacity building of national an local actors

description.narrative: This concerns capacity building such as training and on the job support to national and local actors. This is captured under "Capacity building local partners" in the DRA budget. Please divide Capacity building local partner costs by the Grand Total Budget (incl. ICR) to calculate this percentage. Note that this does not include local offices of INGOs.

comment.narrative: 2% of the budget will be used to strenghten the capacity of local partners

title.narrative: Unconditional and unrestricted cash (CSH-I1)
Number of people benefitting from unconditional and unrestricted cash transfers

description.narrative: Unconditional transfers are provided to beneficiaries without the recipient having to do anything in return in order to receive the assistance . Unrestricted transfers can be used entirely as the recipient chooses i.e. there are no restrictions on how the transfer is spent (Definitions of CALP). It can be delivered e.g. through local banks, shops, traders, local money transfer companies, remittance companies and post offices in either one or several instalments. Please include in the activity description the amount and frequency of cash transfers (i.e. how often). In case beneficiaries receive multiple transfers (e.g. each month), please only count the beneficiaries once.

comment.narrative: Provision of multipurpose cash assistance to vulnerable households in targeted areas to address acute food insecurity and urgent basic needs, aligned with agreed minimum expenditure benchmarks. Targeting is based on community-defined vulnerability criteria, with safeguards to reduce negative coping strategies and ensure cash for minors is provided through their parents/guardians.

title.narrative: Gender based violence (Prevention, response, other) (PRO-I11)
Number of advocacy products produced and disseminated AND/OR number of meetings/events held

description.narrative: 1) Advocacy may be conducted in the public or non-public sphere. 2) Advocacy products might be notes, briefs, reports, articles, documentaries, films, radio programs; provided that these aim to change policy, behaviour or practice.3) Advocacy might likewise be conducted by holding meetings with duty-bearers, perpetrators or influencers; or by events (conferences, meetings, exhibitions).4) In the activity description field, describe what constitutes an advocacy product or event in the context of the action, and the expected effect of the advocacy action.5) In reporting reflect on the effect of the advocacy initiative.

comment.narrative: Community-based GBV prevention and response through awareness-raising, community dialogues, peer support groups, and distribution of information materials, with a strong focus on children, adolescents, and vulnerable households. Strengthening GBV systems via trainings on risks and safe referral pathways, establishment of safe spaces, improved incident monitoring and referral follow-up, and reinforced SEA/PSEA protection mechanisms, informed by risk assessments, community-led risk mapping, and coordinated case management with service providers and clusters.

title.narrative: Support to separated/unaccompanied children (PRO-I8)
Number of unaccompanied and/or separated children who are reunited with their caregivers OR in appropriate protective care arrangements based on BIA

description.narrative:
1) Care arrangements can include temporary care arrangements in host family or other care arrangements.2) Appropriate means (but is not limited to) that care arrangements must take into account different needs of children based on their age, sex and diversity. Morevoer they must as much as possible be defined taking into account the specificities of the context and - when appropriate - be built on existing coping mechanisms. 3) Appropriate is related to the physical safety and psychosocial well-being of the child. Specific attention should be put on non-discrimination of fostered children compared to biological ones. 4) Unaccompanied and/or separated children must be disaggegated by age and sex.
This indicator excludes the reunification of other family members (above 18) which is to be reported under PRO-R14

comment.narrative: Identification and case management of unaccompanied and separated children, including registration, best interest assessments, and the full IDTR process (documentation, tracing, and reunification) to ensure safe and durable protection solutions. Provision of safe alternative care when reunification is not possible, with coordination among authorities and child protection actors and continuous monitoring and follow-up, ensuring approaches are age-, gender-, and diversity-sensitive and aligned with child protection standards.

title.narrative: Prevention and response to violence (PRO-I1)
Number of persons reached by the implementation of specific prevention measures

description.narrative:
1) Preventive measure must be built on a thorough analysis of the risks and should - as much as possible - be designed to provide concrete changes in the short/medium term. Changes must be measured in the course of the action. Preventive measure should focus on the increased risks resulting from the crisis, rather than more structural issues. 2) Use the activity description field to describe what measures are foreseen (sensitisation, infrastructure, etc.).3) Number of persons reached by prevention measures must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.4) If action also includes response activities, please add a custom indicator to reflect this.
Please note that prevention of GBV is captured under PRO-I11.

comment.narrative: Community-based sensitization on protection and GBV prevention through trainings for community and faith leaders, targeted awareness sessions in schools and communities, and wider community campaigns. Support to survivors through referral pathways, plus dissemination of GBV prevention messages via IEC materials and local radio, including capacity building on SGBV, child protection, and safeguarding.

title.narrative: Gender based violence (Prevention, response, other) (PRO-I12)
Number of persons reached by the implementation of specific GBV prevention measures

description.narrative: 1) Preventive measure must be built on a thorough analysis of the risks and should - as much as possible - be designed to provide concrete changes in the short/medium term. Changes must be measured in the course of the action. Preventive measure should focus on the increased risks resulting from the crisis, rather than more structural issues. 2) Use the activity description field to to describe what measures are foreseen (sensitisation, infrastructure, etc.).3) Number of persons reached by prevention measures must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.4) If action also includes response activities, please add a custom indicator to reflect this.

comment.narrative: Survivor-centred GBV response delivered through mobile GBV teams, community alert/referral mechanisms, and Women and Girls Safe Spaces, ensuring confidential intake, case management, and coordinated referrals with health, legal, protection, and mental health services. Provision of psychosocial support (including psychological first aid and individual/group sessions), timely referral for clinical management when needed, strengthened MHPSS programming for children and caregivers, and socio-economic reintegration support for women and girl survivors through skills training, mentoring, and reintegration assistance.

title.narrative: Protection information dissemination (PRO-I5)
Number of persons with increased/appropriate information on relevant rights and/or entitlements

description.narrative: 1) Protection information dissemination refers to provision of information as opposed to actual training or capacity building on protection; as such this will normally target larger numbers than capacity building, and will not involve testing of increased knowledge.2) Relevant rights and entitlements must be defined and should be closely linked to actual risks faced be the targeted group as a result of the crisis.3) Entitlements refers (but is not limited to) availability and accesibility of services (both provided by humanitarian agencies and other actors).4) In activity description field the target group of dissemination (population/authorities/AFs/AGs, etc.) should be clarified.5) In activity description field define focus of information (Rights and access to services awareness, including child-specific measures, Sensitisation campaigns/Risk awareness; IHL/IHRL dissemination).6) Number of persons must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.

comment.narrative: Prevention and community mobilisation activities to strengthen child protection awareness, risk reduction, and safe referral within communities. Development and dissemination of communication tools that clearly explain referral service pathways so communities know where and how to access support.

title.narrative: Child Protection (PRO-I15)
Number of children that received support specified to their needs

description.narrative:
1) This indicator covers response to children (girls and boys under 18). 2) Appropriate response is defined as the provision of comprehensive services/assistance based on a thorough analysis of the risks faced by persons. The protection outcome of the response must be well defined. Relevant SOPs (including functional Referral Mechanism) should be followed. 3) Use the activity description field to to describe what services (medical, MHPSS, legal, security, etc.), as well as SOPs are in place. Activities can include psychosocial support to children, Child Friendly Spaces and support to parents to fulfill their protection responsibilities towards their children. 4) Number of persons must be disaggregated by sex at reporting stage.5) If action also includes prevention activities, please describe this within the activity under this indicator.
If relevant, please specify in the activity description your target population, for example child soldiers.

comment.narrative: Comprehensive child protection prevention and response through community mobilisation, sensitisation on child wellbeing, and the set-up of mobile Child-Friendly Spaces providing emergency psychosocial support and age-/gender-sensitive activities. Individual child protection case management and follow-up based on risk assessments, including distribution of dignity kits and referral to specialized services (health, nutrition, education, and GBV), supported by trained case workers, updated referral pathways, and standardized inter-agency tools and procedures.

title.narrative: Prevention and response to violence (PRO-I2)
Number of persons who receive an appropriate response

description.narrative:
1) This indicator covers response to people (adults and children) having been victims of all kinds of violence. If the response provided is solely for suvivors of GBV, please select the GBV sub-sector.2) Appropriate response is defined as the provision of comprehensive services/assistance based on a thorough analysis of the risks faced by persons. The protection outcome of the response must be well defined. Relevant SOPs (including functional Referral Mechanism) should be followed.3) Use the activity description field to describe what services (medical, MHPSS, legal, security, etc.) are foreseen, as well as the SOPs in place.4) Number of persons must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.5) If action also includes prevention activities, please add a custom indicator to reflect this.
Please note that response to GBV is captured under PRO-I12.

comment.narrative: Comprehensive GBV survivor support through case management, including referral to medical services when needed, psychosocial support, legal aid, and targeted cash-based assistance for dignity needs. GBV risk prevention and mitigation at community level by strengthening local protection structures to conduct regular awareness and risk-reduction activities, ensure safe identification and referrals through SOPs, and operate help desks for GBV-related assistance and referrals, with ongoing monitoring of changes in knowledge and practices.

title.narrative: Individual household shelter (SHL-I1)
Number of people having access to basic, safe and dignified shelters solutions

description.narrative: Basic, safe and dignified: - affected individuals have an minimum covered floor area of 3.5m2 per person. - all shelter solutions and materials meet locally agreed technical and performance standards and are culturally acceptable. - all household (re-)construction is in accordance with safe building practices and standards. - all household (re-)construction demonstrate involvement of the affected population and/or are culturally acceptable by the affected population.

comment.narrative: Identification of targeted households for emergency shelter assistance in the intervention areas. Procurement and distribution of emergency shelter kits to vulnerable households to support immediate safe and dignified temporary accommodation.

title.narrative: Non-food items (SHL-I4)
Number of people provided with non-food items (other than hygiene/dignity kits)

description.narrative: Distribution of Non-Food Items. All household materials excluding those that fall under hygiene/dignity kits or direct shelter items. Also excludes unrestricted cash, which is to be put under indicator CSH-I1 or CSH-I2. However, if cash is provided for the purpose of buying household items, it should be put under this indicator (i.e. restricted cash).

comment.narrative: Distribution of essential non-food item kits to vulnerable households to meet immediate basic needs. Kits include core household items for cooking, sleeping, water storage, and daily use to support safe and dignified living conditions.

title.narrative: Water supply (WSH-I4)
Number of people having access to sufficient and safe water for domestic use

description.narrative: Access: maximum distance to water point 500m, queuing time less than 15min, filling time maximum 3 min/20 litres or as locally agreed. Water access should be during the whole period of implementation unless action is mostly related to building the local water delivery capacity. Sufficient: covering basic needs, i.e. 7.5-15 l/p/d or as locally agreed. Safe: 1) low risk of faecal contamination, 2) No faecal coliforms detectable in any 100-ml sample, 3) For piped water supplies, or for all water supplies at times of risk or presence of diarrhoea epidemic, water is treated with a disinfectant to achieve free chlorine residual at the tap of 0.5 mg per litre and turbidity is below 5 NTU, 4) If for a short period, water which is contaminated chemically or radiologically is used, no (significant probability of) negative health effect is (likely to be) detected. Domestic use: drinking, cooking and personal hygiene (incl. laundry)

comment.narrative: Quick repairs to damaged water pipes and taps to restore and increase water supply in affected areas, with interim water trucking to maintain uninterrupted service during works. Installation of water points and storage near supported health facilities, provision of handwashing stations with soap, and chlorination at key water collection points to improve water safety and hygiene.

title.narrative: Excreta disposal (WSH-I2)
Number of people having access to dignified, safe, clean and functional excreta disposal facilities

description.narrative: Access: ratio (user/facility) of 1 toilet for a max. 20 people, distance < 50 metres from dwellings, or as locally agreed. Clean: regular cleaning and maintenance for public facilities. Dignified: Use of toilets respect cultural preference and is arranged by household(s) and/or segregated by sex. Unsafe facilities: unstable (unlined) pits with risk of collapse, pits accessible to vectors, pits contaminating water tables and poorly sited facilities which expose women and girls to attacks, especially at night. Functional facility: fully constructed, in working order and properly maintained, of a type and in a location acceptable to intended users, with hand washing facilities and anal cleansing material.

comment.narrative: Construction, rehabilitation, and installation of gender-segregated emergency latrines and showers in high-density return and displacement areas to ensure safe, accessible, and private facilities for women and girls. Support to vulnerable households through the installation of emergency sanitation and bathing facilities to improve hygiene and dignity at household level.

title.narrative: Hygiene promotion (Awareness) (WSH-I6)
Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities. Could be training, campaigns, radio broadcasts, flyers etc. Excludes the distribution of Hygiene/dignity kits that should be covered under WHS-I1.

comment.narrative: Hygiene promotion and IPC sensitization in communities and health facilities, delivered in local languages with gender and inclusivity mainstreamed, including awareness on GBV themes and WASH-related gender norms. Capacity building through training community health volunteers and running community awareness sessions and campaigns to improve hygiene and sanitation practices and reduce disease transmission.

title.narrative: Hygiene promotion (WSH-I1)
Number of people having regular access to soap to meet hygienic needs

description.narrative: Regular and timely access: 250g soap/p/m for personal hygiene, 200g soap/p/month for laundry. This includes hygiene/dignity kits. Access may be in-kind or though voucher distribution or through unconditional restricted cash to enable beneficiary to buy soap (without compromising access to other basic needs). Distributed items need to be culturally acceptable i.e. take into account local practice and expectations.

comment.narrative: Distribution of hygiene, dignity, and WaSH kits to vulnerable households, including water containers, essential hygiene items, and water purification support. Identification of women and girls in need and provision of MHM dignity kits, alongside latrine and environmental cleaning kits for households and community focal points.
